subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Who Is Liable After a Breach?
description: A quick win: understand Who Is Liable After a Breach?.

hook.text: A company gets breached. Who pays? The company? The CISO? The board? The vendor? The answer is: all of them.

buildup.text: Liability after a breach can fall on the company, its officers, vendors, and even auditors who missed red flags.

discovery.text: Class action lawsuits from breach victims regularly settle for hundreds of millions of dollars.

twist.text: Directors and officers can be personally sued if they ignored known cyber risks.

climax.text: Breach liability now reaches the boardroom. Ignoring cyber risk isn't just negligent — it's legally risky.

punchline.text: Everyone's liable. The board, the CISO, the vendor.

quiz.question: Can board members be personally liable after a breach?
options: Yes, if they ignored known cyber risks
No, only the IT team is liable
Only if they personally caused the breach
